key: Night of Prayer for the Moon
0.content:
Moon-Prayer Night (also: Kuunrukous, Night of Prayer for the Moon, Moon-Prayer Night festival): Moon-Prayer Night (Kuunrukous, "moon-prayer") is a festival in Nod-Krai held on the night the moon comes closest to Teyvat. The Frostmoon Scions began it to celebrate the birth of the Moon Goddess; over time it became Nod-Krai's liveliest festival. Today most townsfolk treat it as a local custom and a chance to do business rather than a religious rite.

Its timing is never fixed in advance. People guess roughly, then wait for signs: the crescent at the top of the Verdant Crests turns into a full moon and the Moon-Prayer Blossoms bloom with a special radiance, which Nod-Kraians take as blessed omens. Because the moon is so close, kuuvahki reaches its peak. The waiting is part of the fun.

The festival is a story setting in Version 6.2, when the Traveler and Paimon prepare and attend it in Nasha Town with Columbina, who has never joined a Moon-Prayer Night before.

Practice: In the Scions' past tradition, participants wore Moon-Prayer Blossoms, celebrated the Moon Goddess's birth with song and dance, and prepared food and handicrafts to give to others. In Nasha Town today, Moonveils are hung from buildings so that the night sky looks misty through them, Verdant Crests are set up, and stalls sell festival treats such as Moon-Prayer Candy in many flavours.

In the Version 6.2 celebration, the Frostmoon Scions' area has Lauma's wishing slips, where people hang written wishes, plus sugar sculptures and balloon animals; Lauma also invites friendly animals. The Hexenzirkel runs a section of games and prizes with Alice, Barbeloth and Nicole, with Varka and Albedo taking part. Nasha Town's own stalls include candy, a frostfin whale game and a concentration game involving Kuuhenki. Katheryne wishes adventurers a happy Moon-Prayer Night.

Regional variation: The festival is tied to Nod-Krai and described mainly in Nasha Town. Katheryne notes that most people there see it as a business opportunity and do not concern themselves with the religious element, while the Frostmoon Scions keep a closer tie to the Moon Goddess. Lauma calls it a long-held tradition of Nod-Krai.

Scene use: Use it for lively, warm scenes: crowds, stalls, misty Moonveils over the night sky, candy, wishes pinned up by children, mage games. A Nasha Town local may mention it casually or commercially; a Frostmoon Scion may speak of it with more reverence. Do not give it a fixed date or ritual set beyond what is stated here.

Before the festival, expect talk of waiting for the omens and of mirage-like phantoms appearing around Nod-Krai. After the Version 6.2 events, it can carry bittersweet weight for characters connected to Columbina, who says she wishes it could last longer than one night.

History: The Frostmoon Scions first celebrated it, and it has been a long-held tradition in Nod-Krai since. It is celebrated in the Version 6.2 Archon Quests In the Shifting Light of the Moon and The Night the Moon Returns Home, part of the Song of the Welkin Moon chapter, where the festival and the phantoms around it drive the plot.

1.comment: Moon-Prayer Night: Moon-Prayer Blossoms and Verdant Crests
1.content: At the festival's peak, the crescent moon at the top branches of the Verdant Crest turns into a full moon and Moon-Prayer Blossoms bloom with unusual radiance. Nod-Kraians read these as blessed omens, and they guide the timing of the festival. Canon links the effect to the moon's closeness and to kuuvahki reaching its peak.

2.content: Cloth hung from buildings in Nasha Town during the festival. Looking at the night sky through it gives a lovely misty effect. Sarakka is seen checking whether one is translucent enough.

3.content:
Nod-Krai Cuisine (also: Nod-Kraian cuisine, Nod-Krai food, Nod-Kraian food, Nod-Krai dishes, Nod-Kraian dishes): Nod-Krai food is warming, practical frontier cooking with a clearly Nordic flavour. Staples are salmon chowder (Lohikeitto), rye bread and crispbread, smoked fish and meat, sausages in bread (the Nod-Krai Hot Dog), and sweets built on wild berries, above all pale Lakkaberries in krumkakes and pies. The region's main restaurant is Speranza in Nasha Town, run by Katya.

The cuisine is known in game through item descriptions, shop pages and a few quests rather than a single cultural write-up, so this entry sticks to what those texts say.

Practice: Cold, short days and a scrap-built frontier shape the menu: food is filling, keeps well, and leans on fish, cured and smoked meat, rye and berries. Dishes named in canon:
- Lohikeitto: described as a classic soup of the frigid regions. Salmon chunks and fresh vegetables are cooked together, and cream goes in just before serving for a silky chowder.
- Nod-Krai Hot Dog: a sausage in bread with fried onions and sauce, called classic convenience food. Katya's stall call advertises it fresh out of the oven.
- Lakkaberry Krumkakes: a classic dessert; batter is cooked on a griddle and rolled up fast, with butter and fruit added. Item text says it is very popular among children.
- Lakkaberry Madame: a sweet-and-sour chopped chicken dish, said to have become really popular in Nod-Krai though its recipe was imported. Its name hints at the Mondstadt dish Sweet Madame.
- Lakkaberry Pie: once made from Lakkaberries alone, later enhanced with Midsommar Berries, but the name never changed. It is a beloved staple on Nod-Krai tables.
- Midsommar Torte: a small baked cake with berry jam, Smetana and a berry on top, a popular surprise on festival days.
- Smoked Fish Steak: fish cured, laid on a wooden slat and smoked, so it keeps its shape and gains a smoky taste.
- Meat-Filled Rye Bun: a boned fish wrapped in bacon, sealed in thick rye dough and baked; the thick bread keeps the fish juicy.

More dishes:
- Crispy Roast: scored, marinated meat baked in an oven, with simple ingredients and authentic flavour.
- Borderland Crispbread: dry rye crispbread stamped with Icy Pebbles, with a central hole said to imitate them; it has almost no moisture and stores well.
- Birch-Steamed Pork Ribs: ribs marinated, air-dried and steamed on birch branches until tender with a woody scent; the text calls it one of Nod-Krai's traditional festive dishes.
- Berries and Fried Meat: thin fried-then-stewed meat over mashed potatoes, usually eaten with crushed berries.
- Veggie Pot Soup: a mild vegetable soup with light seasoning.
- Berry Herbal Candy: a translucent candy of local flowers, herbs and berries that brings a little brightness to the frozen plains.

Fireside Merriment is a platter of hearty meat cuts that mixes Snezhnayan cured meats with Nod-Krai ham and sausage; many older locals reportedly enjoy it by the fire with a drink. Frontier Land is a layered non-alcoholic drink sold at The Flagship, said to be inspired by Nod-Krai itself, icy at first, then smoky and astringent; the text adds that the alcoholic version is a daily staple of many veteran adventurers. Lakkaberries and Midsommar Berries are wild cooking ingredients (see the berry entry), so many sweets depend on foraging in the warmer parts of the islands.

Regional variation: Nod-Krai is nominally Snezhnayan and its food overlaps with Snezhnaya's rye, Smetana and cured-meat tradition (see the Snezhnaya cuisine entry), but the islands have their own fish, salmon soup, smoked steaks and wild berries. The Frostmoon Scions tradition touches the table as well: Lakkaberry item text says that in their legends the fruit is a gift of the Moon Maiden, like kuuhenki, and that sharing and eating Lakkaberries is a way of worshipping Kuutar. Midsommar Berries symbolise life and abundance in the same legacy because they flourish only in spring and summer. Lakkaberries grow on Hiisi Island and Lempo Isle, particularly near Starsand Shoal; Midsommar Berries mostly in the south of Lempo Isle. Per the wiki, an NPC named Gorchakova indicates they are rare in Snezhnaya.

The Midsommar Berry text also mentions a tale of the King of Winter Icelea and the King of Midsommar Oak, twin monarchs who slay each other as seasons change; the text says most Snezhnayan scholars treat it as a primitive metaphor for the seasons. Use it as folklore, not as a documented festival.

Scene use: Use Nod-Krai meals to show a rough but welcoming borderland: a bowl of creamy Lohikeitto after wind and snow, a hot dog bought from Speranza's counter, a rye bun or crispbread in a travel pack, a plate of Lakkaberry Krumkakes offered by a friend. Katya's restaurant is also a refuge for street children, and meals there come with work and shelter. Do not invent prices, rituals or recipes beyond the item texts.

Contrast settings: the Flagship's rowdy drinks and Frontier Land; Speranza's family-like dining room and Conch Gang kids; a Lightkeeper's or Ratnik's plain field ration; a craftshop where fresh Lakkaberries matter more than market ones. Meals are good vehicles for small kindnesses, such as Katya treating friends of Maite, or Ineffa fetching fresh berries for Aino.

Examples: Nod-Krai Hot Dog, Lohikeitto, Lakkaberry Krumkakes, Lakkaberry Madame, Lakkaberry Pie, Midsommar Torte, Crispy Roast, Smoked Fish Steak, Meat-Filled Rye Bun, Borderland Crispbread, Birch-Steamed Pork Ribs, Berries and Fried Meat, Veggie Pot Soup, Berry Herbal Candy, Fireside Merriment and the drink Frontier Land.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 these dishes are an established part of Nod-Krai life in game. Nothing in canon through 7.1 turns the cuisine into a formal tradition.

4.content: A classic soup of the frigid regions: salmon chunks and fresh vegetables cooked together, with cream and seasoning added just before serving for a smooth, warming chowder. Katya sells the recipe at Speranza. A Knights of Favonius member, Lohen, remembers eating it in Nod-Krai and wonders if he will taste it again after returning to Mondstadt.

5.content:
A classic Nod-Krai dessert: griddle-cooked batter rolled quickly, then buttered and topped with fruit, crisp and sweet. In the anecdote Ineffa: A Matter of Krumkakes, Ineffa picks Lakkaberries at the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop because Aino prefers krumkakes made with fresher berries than the market's that day. Finishing the anecdote gives the recipe. The craftshop itself began with Aino's research on the world's best krumkake machine before becoming a renowned machine workshop.

Per the item text, the pastry is especially popular with children.

6.content: Speranza, in Nasha Town on Lempo Isle, is the main restaurant of Nod-Krai and the home base of the Conch Gang. Its owner Katya is a former Treasure Hoarders adventurer who retired after injuries. She takes in children left on the streets, giving them shelter, food and work; Aino was once one of them. Speranza also has a chef, Jurva, hosts such as Maisie and Mikko, and a luck wheel whose fortunes are told by "Hot Dog". Katya sells the hot dog, Lakkaberry Madame, torte and roast daily, plus recipes and ingredients weekly. A 10% discount applies once the quest Rest Beyond Reach is completed.

7.content: An unmarked world quest at Final Night Cemetery, Paha Isle. A peculiar cooking pot there hosts a food-obsessed phantom chef who says he is making rations for the island's Ratniki. Over three real-time days he sets the Traveler to cook a Nod-Krai Hot Dog (make the bread thicker, add more meat), Berries and Fried Meat (balance meat with berries) and Lakkaberry Madame. At the end he admits he had prepared for the Wild Hunt's arrival but the food was spilled before it could be sent. The reward is the Smoked Fish Steak recipe. His complaints state the priority: plentiful, balanced food matters more than fancy dishes.

8.comment: Nod-Krai Cuisine: Lakkaberry and Midsommar Berry
8.content: Lakkaberries are pearl-white, refreshingly sweet berries growing in threes; in Frostmoon Scions legend they are a gift of the Moon Maiden, a symbol blessed by the new moon, so sharing and eating them is a way to worship Kuutar. Midsommar Berries grow in warmer parts of Nod-Krai and are loved by animals coming out of winter and by children; in the Frostmoon legacy they stand for life and abundance since they flourish only in warm seasons.

9.content:
Daily Life in Nod-Krai (also: Nod-Kraian daily life, everyday life in Nod-Krai, life in the borderlands, Nod-Kraian customs): Daily life in Nod-Krai, the moon-blessed autonomous borderland at Snezhnaya's southern edge, is a frontier life. There is no Archon and no real government. Nasha Town, a port built mostly of scrap metal and crossed by cargo rails, is both a paradise of freedom and a lawless jungle, and people from many nations end up there. The Voynich Guild keeps trade orderly, the volunteer Lightkeepers fight the Wild Hunt, and the Frostmoon Scions keep the old moon customs. Days are short, nights are long, and kuuvahki machines are everywhere.

Visitors call the region an "Elysium," and the word cuts both ways: it promises opportunity and escape, but the land is also hostile, with limited resources and few protective or regulating forces apart from the Voynich Guild. Anyone suspected of carrying a lot of Mora becomes a target, and newcomers are warned to be wary.

For scenes, the best tone is practical, wry and a little patched together: improvised machines, a deal struck under a guild stamp, a story told over a meal, and a quiet awareness that the Wild Hunt is never far.

Three facts shape everyday attitudes. First, nobody can rely on a state: the Voynich Guild, the Curatorium of Secrets, the restaurant Speranza and the Fatui all influence Nasha Town, and none governs it. Second, everyone lives close to kuuvahki, the moon-power that predates the seven elements, so machines and customs revolve around it. Third, the Abyssal Wild Hunt has plagued the land since the Cataclysm, so ordinary people lean on the Lightkeepers even when they do not join.

Practice: Common routines: trade and haggling in Nasha Town, repairing and building kuuvahki machines, buying and selling information, patrol and watch duty for the Lightkeepers, and keeping lanterns and Tideseal Stones in good order against the Wild Hunt.

Nasha Town is the centre of ordinary life. It sits on Lempo Isle as Nod-Krai's main port and commercial centre. Because resources are limited it is built largely of scrap metal; it is also highly industrialised, with cargo rails overhead and kuuvahki-powered machines on every corner. Everyday places include the Adventurers' Guild branch (Katheryne at reception, Sarin as branch master), Mimisbrunnr Books (owner Dhabit; the stock does not refresh and each book can be bought once), the Rossum Workshop smithy (owner Arkhyp, now operated by his daughter Lyulka), the restaurant Speranza (run by Katya, the region's main restaurant and the home base of the "Conch Gang"), the tavern The Flagship and a Northland Bank branch.

Authority is informal. The Voynich Guild, a guild of local merchants based in Nasha Town, is the nearest thing Nod-Krai has to a regulator: it manages trade deals, imports and exports, issues business certificates, investigates and settles disputes, and backs the development of certain technologies. Beside it stands the Curatorium of Secrets, a commission agency that fronts the Northern Intelligence Network, an underground volunteer forum where information is traded for payment.

The Lightkeepers are the defence. They are volunteers who swear a shared oath, carry Oath Lanterns that other members can detect, and answer Wild Hunt incursions wherever they appear. Their headquarters, Piramida, is a city on top of an ancient castle, with a mead hall on its top level where banquets follow hard-won victories. They have set Tideseal Stones across the region to push back the Wild Hunt.

Machines are part of the household. Kuuvahki appears in two forms: polarised, shown as blue or red, whose objects attract or repel each other, and unpolarised, found in the north, which opposes Abyssal energy. People cope by building. The Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop on Lempo Isle, home of the young inventor Aino and her automaton Ineffa, is the source of small bots and of the cannon that guards Nasha Town. Amazing 'Bots roam Lempo Isle and cleaning bots can be controlled from panels on Paha Isle.

Information is a currency. The Curatorium takes commissions from anyone; the network behind it is loosely structured with few rules, and many members gave up positions, reputations, even names to join. Nefer, the Curatorium's owner, is also a member of the Voynich Guild, and the Curatorium's headquarters stands directly behind the Guild's. Adventurers such as Nefer and Jahoda can gather intel on Nasha Town's people and trade it at the Adventurers' Guild.

Lightkeeper life: the group is led by the Starshyna and organised into Sergeant Majors, Squad Leaders and ordinary fighters called Ratniki, who are all volunteers. A Ratnik named Dori says not all members share the same obligations, so many consider early retirement or quitting. Ratniki who break direct orders can be reprimanded, and a member too injured for field duty may be given another role if they still want to serve, as with the doctor Ivar. Squads have names, for example the "Nightmare Orioles," who keep watch over Kipumaki Cliff from Cliffwatch Camp.

Regional variation: Nasha Town on Lempo Isle: busy, industrial and mixed. Hiisi Island, a short way across the water: forest, the Frostmoon Enclave and the Scions' quiet, devout community. Piramida: a fortress-city of volunteers and veterans. Paha Isle: home of the Fatui-built Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau. The north (Voidsea Outlook, Wavechaser Plain, Ashveil Peak, Kipumaki Cliff): Abyssal blight and hazards that need lanterns, spirit blooms and Lightkeeper cover.

South and north differ in how kuuvahki behaves and in how people live with the Abyss. In the north, Oath Lanterns charged with kuuvahki currents reduce the effects of Abyssal Decay, and so do allied Lightkeepers standing nearby. In the southern isles (Lempo, Hiisi, Paha) the lanterns are tied to the Lightkeepers' Oath quest. The Wild Hunt rarely travels to Hiisi Island because the moon's power deters it.

Scene use: Good scene hooks: a scrap-metal market stall, a Voynich stamp someone needs before a deal, a quiet commission at the Curatorium, a Lightkeeper patrol returning to Piramida for a meal, an engineer testing a new kuuvahki gadget, a fortune wheel at Speranza, a boat to Hiisi Island, lanterns lit against a misty night.

Keep the tone wry rather than grim. People joke, haggle and trade favours, and they do not expect officials because there are few. Do not turn Nod-Krai into a place where everyone is a criminal: most residents are merchants, workers, engineers, adventurers and volunteers who chose a hard land. Keep the Wild Hunt as a background danger, and do not give the Lightkeepers or the Scions a single collective personality beyond what canon shows.

Examples: A merchant stamps a certificate and slides it across the counter without looking up. A Ratnik hangs an Oath Lantern by her door before the evening mist. A young engineer tests a hand-built bot on the quay while a neighbour watches. A Scions adherent in a street draped with Moonveils hands over a handmade gift.

10.comment: Daily Life in Nod-Krai: Nasha Town
10.content:
Nasha Town is the seaside port and commercial heart of Nod-Krai, on Lempo Isle. It has no official governing body and is influenced by the Voynich Guild, the Curatorium of Secrets, Speranza and the Fatui. It is mostly built of scrap metal, heavily industrial, with cargo rails overhead and kuuvahki machines throughout. Residents and visitors include merchants, sailors, repairmen, engineers, adventurers, Frostmoon Scions adherents, Fatui soldiers and a Fontaine Research Institute researcher. "Nasha" comes from a Slavic word meaning "our."

Notable places: the Adventurers' Guild branch, Mimisbrunnr Books, Rossum Workshop, Northland Bank, Speranza (run by Katya), the tavern The Flagship, Nuts 'N' Nuts and the Vesnici Proleca Greenhouse. The central plaza has merchants, specialty sellers and Scions adherents. The wiki intro describes it as both a paradise of freedom and a lawless jungle.

11.comment: Daily Life in Nod-Krai: Voynich Guild
11.content: A guild of local merchants based in Nasha Town and one of Nod-Krai's most powerful factions. It is the nearest thing the region has to a regulatory authority, managing trade deals, imports and exports, business certificates and dispute investigation, and backing some technological development. It works closely with the Curatorium of Secrets; Nefer belongs to both. Tarno is a Guild employee.

12.comment: Daily Life in Nod-Krai: Curatorium of Secrets and the Northern Intelligence Network
12.content:
The Curatorium of Secrets is a commission agency in Nasha Town run by Nefer, with Jahoda as an employee. Behind it is the Northern Intelligence Network, an underground volunteer forum for well-connected people who sell information for payment. The network is loosely structured with few rules, and many members gave up their positions, reputations or names to join. Listed informants include Iratxa, Sarin and Tarno; listed clients include Yelan and Varka.

The Curatorium served as the heroes' base during Song of the Welkin Moon. Its permanent front-desk employee Jahoda is a former Seahook Gang member with a mechanical arm built by Aino, and a lazy black cat called Ashru lounges on the counter.

13.content:
The Lightkeepers are Nod-Krai's volunteer defenders against the Wild Hunt, founded five hundred years ago by Solovei, the first Starshyna, under a royal edict of the Tsaritsa after the Cataclysm. Their insignia is a nightingale holding a burning wick. They are led by a Starshyna (Nikita, per the wiki), with Sergeant Majors, Squad Leaders and ordinary fighters called Ratniki, and are headquartered at Piramida. They are short of members. Illuga leads the "Nightmare Orioles" squad and Flins serves as a Ratnik.

Piramida's top-level mead hall holds banquets after victories, with the first pour offered to the dead. A statue of Solovei the Torchforger stands in the city. Members swear an oath on joining and carry Oath Lanterns so other Lightkeepers can detect them.

14.comment: Daily Life in Nod-Krai: Frostmoon Scions
14.content:
The Frostmoon Scions are the indigenous tribe of Nod-Krai, descended from survivors of the golden realm of Hyperborea. They live around Hiisi Island and the Frostmoon Enclave, led by the Moonchanter Lauma, and are organised by rank (Moonchanter, Priestess, Acolyte, Adherent). They appear to abstain from meat and they carved the Statues of the New Moon.

After Lauma revealed that the visible moon was false, some members left the group. Those who stayed agreed to treat Columbina as herself, not as a goddess. Sandrone later apologised to the Scions for the Fatui's actions and the two sides agreed to take steps to reconcile.

15.comment: Daily Life in Nod-Krai: Moon-Prayer Night
15.content: Moon-Prayer Night is Nod-Krai's liveliest festival, held on the night the moon is closest to Teyvat, when kuuvahki peaks. The date is not known in advance: people estimate it and then wait for the Verdant Crests and Moon-Prayer Blossoms to change, and the waiting is part of the fun. Scions once wore the blossoms, sang and danced to celebrate the Moon Goddess's birth, and gave away food and handicrafts. Today they hang Moonveils on Nasha Town's buildings so the night sky looks misty through them, and most people treat it as a chance to do business. Phantoms of the past appear around the festival.

16.comment: Daily Life in Nod-Krai: Wild Hunt
16.content:
The Wild Hunt is an Abyssal phenomenon, strongest in Nod-Krai, that turns the dead into ghouls. Locals tell folk stories about it, such as a demonic host harvesting souls or the phantoms of an ancient nightmare. The Lightkeepers fight it and have placed Tideseal Stones to repel it. Fae can understand the ghouls' speech.

The Wild Hunt began when Rerir, one of Khaenri'ah's Five Sinners, was torn apart trying to follow his lost lover through a moon gate. After he was expelled from Teyvat, the Abyss made an imitation of Roland to lead it; that form expired during Varka's story quest, and as of 7.1 the Hunt is leaderless but still dangerous.

17.comment: Daily Life in Nod-Krai: Statues of the New Moon
17.content: Giant stone statues placed across Nod-Krai by the Frostmoon Scions in the image of their newborn Moon Goddess. Travellers pray to them for protection. Some were caged in steel by the Fatui.

18.content:
Moon Goddess Faith of Nod-Krai (also: Frost Moon faith, Moon Goddess faith, faith of the Frostmoon Scions, Frostmoon Scions' faith, Kuutar worship, Religion in Nod-Krai): Nod-Krai has no Archon, and its one organised faith belongs to the Frostmoon Scions, a tribe descended from Hyperborea who live on Hiisi Island. They worship the Frost Moon: the dead goddess Canon (Huurrekuutar to them), and her successor the Moon Maiden Kuutar, whom the wider world knows as Columbina. The faith is led by the Moonchanter, currently Lauma.

It is a living faith with a heavy past. The Scions kept the rites of Hyperborea after its fall, prayed for centuries to a goddess who no longer answered, and passed down a prophecy that the Moon Goddess would one day return through a Sacred Heir. About 500 years ago the first Moonchanter, Aila, broke with the older cult, abolished its harshest rites and its Archpriestess office, and reshaped the creed around benevolence, faith and avoiding conflict with outsiders. Kuutar was born in that era, and the Scions took her as their goddess.

Its central tension is between worship and the person worshipped. Kuutar found that her devotees wanted their wishes granted rather than her, and left them. In the Song of the Welkin Moon chapter Lauma tells the Scions that the moon they prayed to belongs to a false sky, and the goddess herself asks to be treated as a person, not a deity. How each Scion answers that is the living drama of the faith as of 7.1.

Practice: The Scions pray to the Frost Moon and the Moon Maiden, sing hymns and Runo, treat kuuvahki as the goddess's sacred blessing, and are led by the Moonchanter. Statues of the New Moon, carved in Kuutar's image, stand across Nod-Krai.

Clergy and ranks: the Moonchanter leads, followed by Priestesses, Acolytes and Adherents (ordinary followers). Adherents train to become Acolytes and must pass an examination on hymns and blessings. A quest states that men of the tribe cannot become Acolytes or Priests. Known Priestesses include Ehrnrooth, Sarakka and Rahetar; Verna is an Acolyte who is trying to change the Scions' stance on kuuvahki devices.

Doctrine and customs: kuuvahki is seen as the Moon Goddess's blessing, so using it for personal gain, including through kuuvahki devices, is blasphemy to traditional Scions. They value benevolence and faith and avoid conflict with outsiders.

Hymns: the book Hymns of the Far North, compiled by Priestess Ehrnrooth, preserves the old prayer songs and Runo, noting which were abolished or rewritten by Aila.

Statues: the Scions carved the Statues of the New Moon in the likeness of the newborn goddess, from fine Lunasoul Stone. The Fatui later caged several of them in steel.

Aila's substitutions show how daily practice changed. Where the old rite for a birth offered sea salt and chanting to a mother-of-life figure, a senior cleric now says "May the new moon illuminate your path" over the child to guard it from the taint of the sublunary sphere. For the dead, regardless of social standing, a cleric of Assistant Priestess rank or higher says "May the new moon lead you to the shore of peace," followed by a simple solemn funeral. The old funerary rite had required animal sacrifices scaled to the dead person's rank. Prayers to nature's wrath were rewritten as plain appeals to the Frost Moon, and the dawnstar prayer was reduced to a short plea for the Frost Moon's protection.

The Scions' home on Hiisi Island, the Frostmoon Enclave, once consisted of towers, fortresses and temples. Aila had them torn down, saving only the pillar raised by Xiuhcoatl, because she believed that isolation fed delusions. The Enclave of today has a Grand Library.

Moon-Prayer Night (Kuunrukous) began as a Scion observance on the night the moon comes closest, when they wore Moon-Prayer Blossoms, sang and danced for the Moon Goddess's birth and gave away food and handicrafts. Today it is mostly a local custom and business occasion across Nod-Krai; the Scions hang Moonveils on Nasha Town's buildings. See its own entry.

History: After Hyperborea fell, the Frost Moon goddess Canon guided survivors to Hiisi Island and died. The Scions kept her faith, which Aila reformed 500 years ago, and then took the newborn Kuutar as their goddess.

Fall and refuge: after the Celestial Nail destroyed Hyperborea, Canon led the survivors to Hiisi Island in Nod-Krai and died. They settled around a pillar raised by Xiuhcoatl, later called the Sanctum of the Oathbearer, and kept their rites even though their prayers went unanswered. A prophecy arose that the Moon Goddess would return through a Sacred Heir born to the tribe.

Aila's reform: about 500 years ago the last Archpriestess, Lovia, pressed the Sacred Heir Project to extremes, and her charge Aila killed her. Aila abolished the Archpriestess office, became the first Moonchanter, ended the old rites and reshaped the hymns. She foresaw Kuutar's birth, and the Scions took Kuutar as the Frost Moon's successor.

Details of the reform: Lovia's twin charges Alia and Aila were made to murder other Scions and drink their blood to raise their purity. Aila sided with the hero Solovei and killed Lovia; Alia died stopping Rotwang's attempt to open a gate to the Abyss. Aila gave Solovei the Arrow of Terpikeraunas, which he used to found the Lightkeepers, and offered the newborn Kuutar the first drop of silver blood. The Scions carved Statues of the New Moon across Nod-Krai in her likeness.

Kuutar soon saw that the Scions cared more about having their desires granted than about her, and when she could no longer answer prayers she left; she later joined the Fatui as Columbina, the Damselette, Third of the Harbingers. The Fatui in turn valued only her power. A few months before the Song of the Welkin Moon events she left them and returned to Hiisi Island, where Lauma apologised for her ancestors and hid her in Silvermoon Hall.

Lauma had realised that the moon in the sky was not the real Frost Moon. Lauma sensed that the remnants of the real Frost Moon lay beyond the False Sky. During the Song of the Welkin Moon chapter (In the Shadows of Night) she told her people the whole truth after long consideration. Some left the Scions for good; those who remained met Columbina and agreed to respect her wish to be treated as herself, not as a goddess.

Regional variation: The faith is centred on Hiisi Island. Elsewhere in Nod-Krai most people are not Scions, and Nasha Town treats Moon-Prayer Night mostly as a business occasion.

Nod-Krai is a borderland of many peoples, none of whom share the Scions' creed. The Lightkeepers, the Voynich Guild and the Curatorium of Secrets are not religious bodies, and the Fatui treated the moons as a source of power rather than an object of worship. Statues of the New Moon are respected landmarks, and the in-game text says travellers pray for protection when they come across one.

The sacred bloodline traits are tribal rather than doctrinal: silver blood, kuuvahki sensitivity, antler crowns (said to have been gifted to the Hyperboreans by the Frost Moon at the end of her life) and the ability to communicate with living things. They run strongest in rare individuals such as Lauma, whose unusual sensitivity is said to come once in a century.

Scene use: Use the Scions as gentle, hospitable and quietly wary of outsiders. Mention hymns, moonlight and kuuvahki; do not make them cultists.

Typical scene beats: a cleric recites a blessing for a child or the dead; Lauma answers a question with a formal blessing; a resident hangs a Moonveil; a Scion hesitates before using a kuuvahki device; someone prays at a Statue of the New Moon. Treat Columbina as a person who lives among them, not as a distant idol, and let the Scions struggle with that.

Distinguish the three audiences: Scions on Hiisi Island who still believe; Nasha Town residents who treat the festival as custom or business; and Fatui who see the moons as resources. Keep the old cult's cruelty in the past: the present Scions condemn Lovia, and her name is known only to higher clergy.

19.comment: Moon Goddess Faith of Nod-Krai: Moonchanter and Scion Ranks
19.content:
The Frostmoon Scions are led by the Moonchanter, a title created by Aila about 500 years ago when she abolished the older office of Archpriestess. Below the Moonchanter are Priestesses, Acolytes and Adherents. Adherents train to become Acolytes and must pass an exam on hymns and blessings. A quest states that men of the tribe cannot become Acolytes or Priests. Lauma is the current Moonchanter; the Priestess Sarakka is the sibling of a previous Moonchanter.

The wiki lists the Priestesses Ehrnrooth, Sarakka and Rahetar; the Acolytes Verna, Zirnytsia and Eveliina; and Adherents including Krodo, Ossian, Reetta, Lyylikki, Kukkia and Kantor. Former members include Vilemina, who cut off her antlers on defecting to the Fatui, and Ryksa. Historical clergy named in the Sanctum texts include Saredne, an Archpriestess in the thirteenth generation after Hyperborea's fall, and Lovia, the last Archpriestess.

20.comment: Moon Goddess Faith of Nod-Krai: Aila's Reforms
20.content:
Aila became the first Moonchanter after she killed Lovia and abolished the Archpriestess office. She ended the ancient Hyperborean rites, rewrote many hymns and tore down the Scions' walls, towers and temples, believing that isolation bred delusion. The faith was to rest on reverence for nature, kindness toward outsiders and benevolence. She erased Lovia from the record and sealed the Court of the First Edict with evidence of Lovia's deeds. Her private notes admit she lied to Solovei when he asked whether she felt hatred.

She also foresaw Kuutar's birth and offered her the first drop of silver blood with Moonweaver's Dawn, and she gave the Arrow of Terpikeraunas to Solovei to found the Lightkeepers. Her own later fate is not stated in the sources read.

21.comment: Moon Goddess Faith of Nod-Krai: Sacred Heir Project
21.content:
A long-term plan to keep the Hyperborean bloodline pure so that the prophesied Sacred Heir could revive Hyperborea. It was modelled on Hyperborea's Seed of Life Project but used eugenics and strict family-tree control, because the old genetic arts were lost. It was meant to be phased out from the seventh generation, but later Priestesses stressed it more. Around 500 years ago a maiden of unusually pure blood, chosen to bear the Heir, eloped with a Snezhnayan officer and bore Avrelian; Lovia had Rotwang retrieve her, and the officer died and she took her own life. The project was then abandoned. The Scions did not regard Avrelian as the Sacred Heir.

Lovia turned instead to twin girls from a lesser branch, Alia and Aila, and forced them to murder other Scions and drink their blood to raise their purity. The Sacred Heir idea persists in the prophecy that the Moon Goddess will return, but no source names a present Sacred Heir.

22.comment: Moon Goddess Faith of Nod-Krai: Hymns of the Far North
22.content:
A three-volume book of hymns and rites passed down among the Scions and compiled by Priestess Ehrnrooth, found at the Frostmoon Enclave. Most of its contents and rites have long fallen into disuse. Each prayer song is preceded by ritual instructions, and Ehrnrooth's notes record how Aila abolished or simplified it. The book mentions sacrifices on the solstices and at harvest. One note observes that the prayer to the Mother of Time describes the Verdant Crest, a tree that appeared at the Moon Maiden's birth five centuries ago, in a rite supposedly older than the tree, and treats it as a scribal error. The fifth song is missing.

Runo are the hymns that structured Hyperborean magic; the first incantations are lost but described as still able to stir change. The book opens with a traveller's lament for a lost homeland, urging Hyperborea's heirs to endure through hymn and Runo.

23.comment: Moon Goddess Faith of Nod-Krai: Statues of the New Moon
23.content:
Giant statues of the newborn Moon Goddess Kuutar, carved by the Frostmoon Scions and found across Nod-Krai. The in-game descriptions say travellers pray to them for protection. During the Fatui's presence, steel cages were built over some of them to harness their power or display Fatui authority. They also serve as the region's worship statues in gameplay.

The gameplay function (offerings and blessings) is a mechanic; in the story they are objects of local reverence and a symbol of who controls Nod-Krai.

24.comment: Moon Goddess Faith of Nod-Krai: Kuutar and the Scions
24.content:
Kuutar is the Scions' name for the Moon Goddess, born about 500 years ago and recognised as the Frost Moon's successor after Canon (Huurrekuutar). The wider world knows her as Columbina, once the Third Fatui Harbinger. She left the Scions because they wanted wishes granted more than they cared for her. After the Song of the Welkin Moon events she goes by Columbina Hyposelenia, asks to be treated as a person, and lives with the Scions on Hiisi Island. Her own biography is in her character entry.

Her presence is divisive: some Scions left the faith when told the truth, while those who remained agreed to respect her wishes. This should be played as a community adjusting, not as unified adoration.

25.comment: Moon Goddess Faith of Nod-Krai: Hiisi Island and the Frostmoon Enclave
25.content: Hiisi Island, in Nod-Krai's Southern Isles, is the Scions' home and the centre of their faith. Much of it is untouched wilderness under their care. The Frostmoon Enclave is the Scions' home area and holds a Grand Library; the Sanctum of the Oathbearer is the surviving pillar from Xiuhcoatl; Silvermoon Hall is a hidden cavern where Lauma hid Columbina to rest.
